sections.html:
Value and payment sit in different hands here. The Property Valuation Administrator (PVA) sets what each parcel is worth, while the sheriff collects the money. Tax rates come from the taxing bodies themselves, including the fiscal court and the school board.

The PVA is at 424 Public Square, Suite 2, Columbia, KY 42728, telephone (270) 384-3673, weekdays eight to four. Deputies there process deed transfers, including partial sales, and adjust vehicle values. The sheriff is at (270) 384-2776 and the County Clerk at (270) 384-2801.

Kentucky fixes values on January 1, so a parcel is appraised as it stood that morning. If you close in February, the year's bill will usually be addressed to the seller, so the sale contract should say who repays whom.

sections.h2: When Adair County tax bills are due
sections.html:
KRS 134.015 sets a payment schedule, and the sheriff collects at each stage.

Payment windowWhat you owe
On or before November 1Face amount less 2 percent
November 2 to December 31Face amount
January 1 to January 31Face amount plus 5 percent
After January 31Face amount plus 10 percent

A late mailing by the state can shift the calendar by one-month blocks. Anything unpaid when collection season closes, April 15 on the normal schedule, is turned over to the County Clerk along with a recorded lien.

sections.h2: What an Adair County owner pays
sections.html:
For 2025 the state rate is 10.6 cents per $100 of assessed value, lower than the 10.9 cents of 2024. That covers the state's share only. County, school and other districts add their own, so the PVA or the sheriff can give you the combined figure for your address.

A payment made by November 1 takes 2 percent off the total. At a sale, someone has to split the year's bill between buyer and seller. Find out how your contract does it, and check with the sheriff on what the account has already paid.

sections.h2: How to challenge an Adair County value
sections.html:
Before any formal appeal, the owner has to meet with the PVA or a deputy. The assessment roll is open for public viewing starting the first Monday in May and for the two weeks after. Bring up a value you dispute then, or sooner if notices have gone out.

  • The PVA owes you an explanation of how the value was reached, and the meeting is recorded in writing.
  • File the appeal with the County Clerk by the workday after viewing ends.
  • Collect evidence: land and building descriptions, insurance papers, construction costs and comparable sales or listings. An appeal without it is denied.
  • Go to the hearing a few weeks later. If you file and do not appear, you lose later review by the Kentucky Claims Commission.

Anyone you pay to represent you must be in a listed group, such as attorneys, CPAs, brokers or certified appraisers, and must carry your written authorization. If the board sets a value above the figure you claimed, a supplemental bill covers the difference.

Owners aged 65 or over, and owners the law treats as totally disabled, get a deduction set by the state Revenue Department at $49,100 for 2025 and 2026. It is subtracted from assessed value before the rate applies.

Send the form to the Adair County PVA in the year you want relief, by mail, fax or email. A driver's license, Medicare card or birth certificate proves age, and a Kentucky license or state ID covers residence. Each household gets one exemption, and it is enough for one spouse to be 65.

Approval lasts as long as the applicant lives in the home as its owner. After a sale, tell the PVA so the exemption comes off the old address and you can request it at the next one.

A sale does not wipe out an overdue balance. Under KRS 134.015 the tax is the owner's personal debt from the assessment date, and the lien stays on the parcel until it is paid or the eleven-year period in KRS 134.420 runs out. Transferring the deed changes nothing. Any title search will find the lien, so get the sheriff's payoff figure before you list.

Once the account is with the County Clerk, interest of 1 percent is added every month. Commissions go to the clerk and the county attorney, and the lien recording fee is tacked on. The owner gets two mailed notices. A certificate may be sold 90 to 135 days after the handoff, and the buyer can add fees.

If you pay the sheriff before April 15, none of those clerk-stage extras apply.

Columbia, the county seat, is also the one incorporated city. Population reached 19,423 in 2025, and 77.2 percent of homes are lived in by their owners. Livestock, dairy, corn and tobacco anchor the farm economy. With only six building permits in 2025, almost every sale is a house that is already built.

Columbia keeps Central time while Taylor and Casey counties to the north run on Eastern, which is worth remembering when you schedule a closing with out-of-county parties.

sections.h2: Paperwork to gather before you sell
sections.html: Have your latest tax bill, the PVA's value notice and the deed ready. If you claim the homestead exemption, note that it needs to be moved or dropped after the sale. If a lien or certificate is already recorded against the parcel, get the figure from the county clerk so the title company can pay it from your proceeds. Clear paperwork makes a buyer's offer faster and a closing smoother.

sections.h2: Steps to close an Adair County sale
sections.html:
First call the sheriff for the account balance and the PVA to confirm the parcel and the owner name on record. With a mortgage open, ask for a payoff figure. The title company will then search for liens, draft the deed and share the year's tax bill with the buyer. Afterward the PVA handles the deed transfer, and a partial sale calls for a copy of the recorded deed.

A house that needs repairs or carries back taxes can be sold for cash as-is, clearing both at one closing. The buyer accepts the present condition, and any unpaid balance comes out of your proceeds at the table.

faqs.q: When is the discount deadline for Adair County property taxes?
faqs.a: November 1 is the cutoff. Pay the whole bill by then and you save 2 percent. The face amount applies through December, and penalties begin in January.

faqs.q: Who takes payment of Adair County tax bills?
faqs.a: The Adair County Sheriff, at (270) 384-2776. The PVA, reachable at (270) 384-3673, only values property and never takes payments.

faqs.q: How much is the homestead exemption in Adair County?
faqs.a: It is $49,100 for 2025 and 2026, taken off the assessed value. Owners who are 65 or older or totally disabled apply at the PVA in Columbia.

faqs.q: Can I appeal my Adair County assessment after the deadline?
faqs.a: No. The PVA conference comes first, and the clerk filing is due the workday after viewing ends. Viewing opens the first Monday of May and runs 13 days.

faqs.q: What happens if Adair County taxes go unpaid?
faqs.a: The county clerk takes over after April 15 and holds a certificate of delinquency backed by a recorded lien. It earns 1 percent interest monthly and may be sold 90 to 135 days after the handoff.
